newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Overwhelming U.N. vote against U.S. Cuba embargo.
newsitem.headline: Overwhelming U.N. vote against U.S. Cuba embargo.

text.p: The General Assembly, for the fifth consecutive year, adopted a resolution by an overwhelming majority on Tuesday calling for an end to the three-decade-old U.S. economic embargo against Cuba.
The vote was 137 to three, with 25 abstentions.
The vote on a similar draft last year was 117 to three, with 38 abstentions. On both occasions the three negative votes were cast by the United States, Israel and Uzbekistan.

As in the past, U.S. allies as well as adversaries voted for the Cuban-sponsored draft because they regard the embargo as violating their own sovereignty by subjecting them to the effects of U.S. laws and regulations.
The 15-nation European Union, some of whose members abstained in the past, voted this time solidly in favor of the resolution.

The criticism of U.S. policy has sharpened because of the latest embargo legislation, the Helms-Burton Act, adopted earlier this year. It allows U.S. citizens who were Cuban nationals before the 1959 communist revolution to sue in U.S. courts foreign companies or individuals who "traffic" in property confiscated by the government of President Fidel Castro.
